notes: AE 1 Displacement Map Layer is the layer reference -> textures.mapTex (role 'map'; textureParams maps it back to AE param 1). Measured model (exact): out(x,y) = bilinear(premultiplied layer, x + dx, y + dy), transparent outside the layer, dx = MaxH*(V-128)/128, dy = MaxV*(V'-128)/128, V = 8-bit value of the chosen map channel at the same pixel (not (V-127.5)/127.5, not 2*(v-0.5)). Popup order 1 Red 2 Green 3 Blue 4 Alpha 5 Luminance 6 Hue 7 Lightness 8 Saturation 9 Full 10 Half 11 Off. Luminance = round(0.299R+0.587G+0.114B) on the straight colour (measured on AE Shift Channels' Luminance, 99.99 % exact; not measured on this effect). NOT measured: Hue/Lightness/Saturation (HLS of the straight map colour), Full/Half/Off taken as constant channel values 255/128/0 (Half = no displacement, Off = -Max, like Shift Channels' constants; if AE's Off actually means 'no displacement', change case 11 to return 128), Wrap Pixels Around (implemented as a modulo wrap of the bilinear taps), Displacement Map Behavior for a map of a different size (Center = centred, no displacement outside the map; Stretch = nearest-scaled map; Tile = modulo) — in the generated Rive node the map artboard is rendered into a layer-sized canvas so textureDimensions(mapTex) == size and the 3 modes coincide. Expand Output (AE 8) only grows the AE layer bounds; with a layer-sized canvas it has no visible effect and with pad > 0 the shader cannot tell the layer rect from the pad (Wrap then wraps around the padded canvas). Map layer effects/masks/transforms: the shader uses whatever the map artboard renders.

measured.rive_run_to_run: Rive screenshots vary between runs by +-1 on ~4 % of pixels (0.001 or 0.008 mean)
